title: Privileged entrypoint never requires authorization
rationale: On Soroban, an address a contract receives is only a claim until `require_auth` is called on it: the host has verified nothing, and nothing about the caller is implied by the arguments. An entrypoint that writes storage or moves value without calling `require_auth` on the address it acts for can therefore be invoked by anyone, for any address, with no signature — the classic unprotected `mint`, `transfer`, `set_admin` or `upgrade`. General Rust tooling cannot see this: the code is well-typed and does exactly what it says, and the missing check is the absence of a call, not a suspicious construct.
remediation: Call `require_auth()` on the address the operation is for, before the effect: `admin.require_auth()` for an administrative action, `from.require_auth()` for a transfer out of `from`'s balance. If the operation is intentionally permissionless, say so in the code with `// soroban-analyzer: allow(soroban-missing-require-auth)` directly above the entrypoint, so the exception is visible in review rather than assumed.
